description_full: Grab Holdings Limited operates the Grab superapp in Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam. The company offers delivery services on its platform, such as GrabFood, a food ordering and delivery booking service; Dine-Out for table reservations; GrabMart, a goods ordering and delivery booking service; GrabAds, an online advertising solution; GrabExpress, a package delivery booking service; Grab for Business platform, a unified management portal for corporate clients. It also provides GrabKios, a network of agents; GrabCar, which enables a private hire driver-partner to register with Grab and accept bookings through its driver-partner application; and GrabTaxi, which enables a taxi driver-partner to register with Grab and accept bookings through the Grab driver-partner application. In addition, the company offers JustGrab, which enables consumers to book a private car or a traditional taxi; GrabBike, a motorcycle ride-hailing offering; three-wheel vehicles for culturally localized modes; carpooling shared mobility options; GrabRentals, which facilitates vehicle rental for its driver-partners; GrabPay, a digital payments solution; and GrabCoins, a loyalty platform. Further, it provides GrabFin for financial services comprising digital and offline lending, PayLater services, white goods financing, receivables factoring, and working capital loans; GrabInsure, aprotection for rides and package deliveries, personal accident insurance, income protection insurance, critical illness insurance, vehicle insurance, and travel insurance; GrabLink, a payment gateway and acquiring service; Digibank Savings Account, a digital banking deposit account. Additionally, the company offers GX Bank debit cards; GXS FlexiCard, a fee-based credit card; and mapping services, autonomous vehicle services, and last-mile delivery infrastructure. Grab Holdings Limited was founded in 2012 and is headquartered in Singapore, Singapore.

financial_summary: Grab Holdings Limited is a large-cap technology business with a $13.8B market cap on $3.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +33% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at -10% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
The company is burning through $18M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 2.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 15% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 2% operating margin trails the Technology median (7%) by 5pp, so it is a below-average operator in its field.
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.08x its revenue share).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 45% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 45% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 40% and a beta of 1.12, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $156.2M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 68% in the 2022 bear market.
val: On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 34.1 vs 26.7 and EV/EBITDA 24.0 vs 16.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of -0.1% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 0.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 23 covering analysts target $5.44 on average, 59% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 10% falls short of the cost of capital of 9.7%, so growth at these returns destroys value.
Earnings quality is a concern: a weak Piotroski score of 3/9 and cash conversion of only 0.40x.
ROE of 3% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 72pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.4B.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 0.18 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 33.0% over 3 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 38%).
own: Insiders own 14.5%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 68%.
Insider trading is two-way: 2 purchases and 12 sales over the past year, net $27.5M bought.
Shareholder yield is a modest 2.0% (2.0% in buybacks).
people: With about 12,012 employees, each generates about $281K of revenue, 0.8x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 49.5% a year.
Free cash flow is negative, at -$1K per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
